As isolated Appalachian communities in Western North Carolina face the worst climate disaster in their history, neighbors must band together in order to survive.

item.title: Which Actor Went the Furthest for a Role?
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
Losing over 60 pounds, learning to box for a year and a half, or hanging off the side of a plane as it takes off. Actors have gone to some ridiculous lengths to make a role feel real.
They’ve transformed their bodies, learned entirely new skills, stayed in character for months, and sometimes put themselves through productions that were almost as demanding as the characters they were playing.
So today, we’re looking at 11 of the most extreme things actors have ever done for a film. But as always, we want to hear from you. Which one do you think went the furthest?

item.title: RICHARD STYLES - Assistant Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 220 Richard Styles - Assistant DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with assistant director Richard Styles (28 YEARS LATER, THE CROWN, GOSFORD PARK). Throughout the episode, Richard helps us understand who is responsible for what, within the assistant directing team, from third to first and all the grades in between. Richard also reflects on getting his shot as a third AD on the endless production of ALIEN 3, and we discuss what he learned working as a runner and office PA in England up until then. We later discuss the puzzle of scheduling, and Richard shares his strategies and experiences for not just locking a schedule but also adjusting it as production unfolds. Richard also reflects on how he helps maintain morale on set, and he shares how he adapts to each new director he works with. Richard also shares how he, director Fernando Meirelles (Season 2, Episode 198), and cinematographer César Charlone (Season 2, Episode 174) shot the global story of THE CONSTANT GARDENER around the world, and Richard gives his advice to anyone interested in working in the film industry. item.title: TIM SQUYRES - Editor
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 219 Tim Squyres - EditorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with editor Tim Squyres (GEMINI MAN; LIFE OF PI; CROUCHING TIGER, HIDDEN DRAGON). Throughout the episode, Tim shares his thoughts on many aspects of editing, with topics ranging from finding the right cut of a scene with the director to dealing with studio notes and screening reactions. Tim also shares how he first met director Ang Lee and why he thinks they've continued to work together since 1991, and we learn how Tim cut films such as CROUCHING TIGER, HIDDEN DRAGON and LUST, CAUTION despite not understanding the film's spoken language. We also learn how Tim adapts his process to different directors, and we discuss how he feels when he receives a mountain of coverage on a scene. Tim, through his work with Ang, has cut a number of films on the edge of technological advancements from 3D projection to elevated framerates, and he shares how the process of cutting those films differs and mirrors the process of cutting a film following a traditional American cinematic format. We also discuss Tim's role as another judge for performance, and Tim shares his involvement in the sound mixing of a movie. Tim edited UNBROKEN (which we shot) and we had a wonderful time catching up with him.This episode is sponsored by BenQ

item.title: Miracle Mile (1988) - re:View
item.author: RedLetterMedia
item.content:encoded: In these trying times of trying, one must ensure his or her ability to try less. Hi, I'm Krebs Gorlon, the official spokesfolk for RLM. In today's video, Mark and Jar talk about a movie that ironically totally dropped off the RADAR (I say ironically because the films main concept is about incoming nuclear missiles) But enough of my endless wit and impeccably funny observations that go over all of your heads... this film is a blast... litera.... eh, forget it. Now the one on the left named Jar brought up this film on a recent trip to Palm Springs with his "pal" Mark. While soaking up some rays and sipping beach-themed cocktails, Jar says, "Hey Mark. Have you ever seen Miracle Mile?" to that Mark replies, "Baby, I haven't. But I've been seeing Miracle 3 inches nearly every night on vacay!" Jar was visibly upset. He threw his cocktail in Marks face and stormed off from the pool area. All the other gays saw the drama and started to gossip. Later that evening, Mark apologized and took his question more seriously. "Jar, with no brains, I'm sorry. I haven't seen Miracle Mile. Is it a movie?" Jar explained to Mark what it was and he was intrigued. He said he'd watch it when they got back. It was too late to watch it tonight because tomorrow they had an early drive out to Los Angeles to visit the Academy Museum of Motion Picture Arts! And as luck would have it, it was the ground zero of the films shooting location (another bomb pun) WHAT ARE THE ODDS!!?? It's as if Jar had planned it!!! THAT SNEAKY QUEEN! So Mark watched the film and really liked it. Now the boys are here to talk about it on a YouTube! It's a hard one to discuss without talking about the major spoiler of it all, but there's lots of goodness to it even if one knows the outcome. What a time is must have been to be alive and make a movie like this in 1988! (I wouldn't know cause I was born in 2005) I don't see old crusty fart movies like this anymore. I don't even watch movies. I play Roblox and watch TikTik videos while I bedrot or whatever. No one would actually watch this crap except for these old, gay grandpas! Ha ha! These two suck! (you see I can write whatever I want this far into the description because I know these two boring old boomer clowns don't even read this far down) So yeah, blah blah blah, whatever whatever description description Mark says 2,500 words and "make it good" - whatever that means. I'd just use ChatGPT to right this, but I wanted to slay these old flabs. That clown Mark, let me tell you about him! That old bag of fat is still trying to fit into XXXL flannel shirts! Give it up and go with the muumuu ! And my god can we talk about those SHORTS?! Keep it to yourself please. The world doesn't want to see your old pasty white old man dead chicken thighs. And Jar, nice palm tree shirt (got it in Palm Springs?) Did he wear that cause of the palm trees on the movie poster? Only one more month until my unpaid internship is over and I can begin my career as a political columnist for the New York Times!

item.title: PETER KOSMINSKY - Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 218 Peter Kosminksy - DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with director Peter Kosminsky (WOLF HALL, THE UNDECLARED WAR, THE STATE). Peter's work as a director encompasses both film and television which covers topics including the Falklands War, ISIS, Thomas Cromwell, and an Emily Brontë novel. Throughout the episode, Peter reflects on the highs and lows of his career, from standing up to the BBC over censorship to being chosen by Hilary Mantel to adapt WOLF HALL for television, and we discuss his general thoughts on directing, casting, and writing. Peter also reflects on his difficult experience directing 1992's WUTHERING HEIGHTS while being undermined by the film's producers, and we discuss how the experience shaped the rest of his career and approach as a director. We later question Peter about his work on THE STATE, a fictional four-part miniseries about ISIS, and we learn how he approached making a show about radicalization and contemporary issues that were actively developing while creating the series. Peter also shares his views on the changing cultural power of television, and we discuss the effects of the rise of streaming services on the economics of creating a series.This episode is sponsored by BenQ
